The physical world needs tuning." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="52" width="460" x="20" y="340" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="why" parent="1" style="rounded=0;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#f3faf1;strokeColor=#82b366;fontSize=11;align=left;spacingLeft=10;verticalAlign=top;spacingTop=8;fontStyle=1" value="Why no LLM in the hot path

An LLM call inside a 30-minute promise is an
outage waiting to happen.

The LLM's role here is OFFLINE:
explain the plan to an operator, and answer
"为什么这单从B仓发货？"
— grounded on stock, distance and split risk." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="220" width="200" x="1570" y="100" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="new" parent="1" style="rounded=0;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#fffdf5;strokeColor=#d6b656;fontSize=11;align=left;spacingLeft=10;verticalAlign=top;spacingTop=8;" value="What has to be created

前置仓 as a location type
 capacity, freezer/ambient zones,
 pick-time model ~2d
3km cell grid + mapping ~1d
rider/fleet model ~2d
weather + local-event feed ~2d
 (weather is a FIRST-ORDER driver
 of instant-retail demand)
OSRM distance matrix per cell ~1d" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="240" width="200" x="1570" y="350" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="tools" parent="1" style="rounded=0;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#f9f9f9;strokeColor=#999999;fontSize=11;align=left;spacingLeft=12;dashed=1;verticalAlign=middle;" value="Components: autogluon/chronos-2 (Apache-2.0) · google/or-tools (Apache-2.0) · Project-OSRM/osrm-backend (BSD-2) · QwenLM/Qwen-Agent (Apache-2.0, explanation only)
Existing services used unchanged: stock-service (per-warehouse stock) · order-service (O2oFulfillmentController, DeliveryLogController) · channel-service · purchase-service" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="80" width="1480" x="40" y="600" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="kpi" parent="1" style="rounded=0;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#f3faf1;strokeColor=#82b366;fontSize=12;align=left;spacingLeft=12;verticalAlign=middle;fontStyle=1" value="THE metric: FULFILMENT COST PER ORDER. Secondary: on-time rate, split rate, substitution rate, orders per rider hour. Holdout by warehouse or by day (I06).
Duoduo Maicai — the one survivor of the community-group-buying war — won on exactly this: per-order fulfilment cost ~¥0.7–1, about 60% below the industry average." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="90" div.div: Market ¥800B (2025) → ¥1T+ (2026). 50,000+ front warehouses nationwide, density +40%. Meituan: 5,000+ 闪电仓, 150M instant orders in a single day. The 3km radius IS the structural advantage.

div.div:
THE LESSON IN THE LOSS NUMBERS
12 months to June 2026:
Alibaba −¥41B
JD −¥26B
Meituan −¥25B EBIT
The platforms are burning cash on SUBSIDIES.
The durable advantage is FULFILMENT COST PER ORDER,
decided by three algorithmic choices.
→ We optimise cost per order.
→ We do NOT model subsidy strategy. Out of scope, explicitly.

div.div:
Why no LLM in the hot path
An LLM call inside a 30-minute promise is an
outage waiting to happen.
The LLM's role here is OFFLINE:
explain the plan to an operator, and answer
"为什么这单从B仓发货？"
— grounded on stock, distance and split risk.

前置仓 as a location type
capacity, freezer/ambient zones,
pick-time model ~2d
3km cell grid + mapping ~1d
rider/fleet model ~2d
weather + local-event feed ~2d
(weather is a FIRST-ORDER driver
of instant-retail demand)
OSRM distance matrix per cell ~1d

div.div:
THE metric: FULFILMENT COST PER ORDER. Secondary: on-time rate, split rate, substitution rate, orders per rider hour. Holdout by warehouse or by day (I06).
Duoduo Maicai — the one survivor of the community-group-buying war — won on exactly this: per-order fulfilment cost ~¥0.7–1, about 60% below the industry average.
